name: Lagrange’s analytical mechanics
description: A generalized-coordinate and variational synthesis of statics and dynamics.

impact.note: Reformulation of existing mechanics so large that theoretical physics reorganised around it; used by physicists and engineers, founding analytical dynamics.

places.note: Place of the 1788 publication; not necessarily where every method originated.

date.basis: Publication year of the first edition; work developed over earlier decades.

events.statement: Lagrange’s Méchanique analitique appeared in Paris in 1788, treating statics and dynamics in an analytical framework.

evidence.supports: Describes generalized coordinates and the earlier development of the analytical approach.
Describes generalized coordinates and the earlier development of the analytical approach.

earliest_record.rationale: The published synthesis is the dated witness for this scoped capability; prior work is not dated by it.

caveats: Generalized coordinates and variational methods evolved over prior decades and built on work by several other mathematicians. Later editions contain additions that should not be attributed to the 1788 edition without inspection.

research.note: The catalogue and historical discussion were read; no claim that the entire original edition was inspected. Independent review checked the event dating and scope against the cited work, historical source, edition metadata or modern translation, as applicable.
